newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour's Clark says hopeful of "govt of change".
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour's Clark says hopeful of "govt of change".

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark acknowledged on Saturday that nationalist New Zealand First would hold the balance of power after the general election and said she hoped it would be possible to form a "government of change".

"It was always going to be the case that New Zealand First was going to hold the balance of power on election night and we are going to have to talk from tomorrow to see whether it is going to be possible to put together a government of change. I very much hope it is," Clark told TV1.

"I certainly will be phoning (NZ First leader Winston) Peters. I will also be phoning (left-wing Alliance leader Jim) Anderton. Clearly a vote of confidence from the Alliance is very important in putting together a new government."
Clark described herself as positive but, asked whether she would become New Zealand's first woman prime minister, said the outcome would depend on coalition talks.
